title: Oral Glucose Tolerance Test in Mice
author: Louise Lantier
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yz2fx8e

steps.title: Prepare Mice and Materials
steps.instruction: Prepare the mice and necessary equipment for the glucose tolerance test.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the mice (note: for mice of differing fat mass, dosing the bolus of glucose on lean mass is recommended, requiring body composition).
Fast mice for 5 hours (7am to 12pm) by transferring them to individual cages or containers.
Prepare an experiment record sheet, glucose measurement sticks, and a syringe for oral gavage of the Dextrose solution.

steps.title: Calculate Glucose Gavage Volume
steps.instruction: Determine the required volume of 20% Dextrose solution for each mouse to achieve a dose of 2g dextrose/kg body mass.

substeps.instruction: Calculate volume using the formula: 20% Dextrose (μl) = 10 x body weight (g).
Record the calculated volume for each individual mouse on the record sheet.

steps.title: Collect Baseline Glucose and Insulin
steps.instruction: Obtain baseline (t = 0) blood glucose and plasma samples.

substeps.instruction: Cut the tail tip using clean surgical scissors and place a small drop of blood (<5μl) on a blood glucose meter test strip; record the result.
Collect 40µL of whole blood in a tube (e.g., Sarstedt’s Microvette® CB 300 cat # 16.443.100 for Heparin or cat # 16.444.100 for EDTA).
Centrifuge the blood for 1min at 13k rpm.
Collect 20µL of plasma in a clean tube and store on ice.

steps.title: Administer Glucose Gavage
steps.instruction: Orally gavage the mouse with the previously determined volume of glucose solution and start the timer.

steps.title: Perform Time-Course Measurements
steps.instruction: Measure blood glucose and collect plasma samples at specified intervals post-gavage.

substeps.instruction: Measure blood glucose levels at 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90, and 120 minutes.
Collect 20µl plasma samples for insulin determination at 10, 30, 60, and 120 minutes.
For each sample, restart bleeding by removing the clot from the first incision or massaging the tail if flow is inadequate.
Place a small drop of blood on a new test strip and record results.
Apply brief pressure to the incision after each measurement to minimize blood loss.

steps.title: Post-Experiment Processing
steps.instruction: Finalize the experiment and store samples.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize mice for tissue collection or place them in a clean cage with food and water available ad libitum for recovery.
Monitor mice for any abnormal behavior.
Store plasma samples in a -20 or -80ºC freezer until analysis.
